threatModel.summary: Experimental offline BIP39 mnemonic encryption/recovery library, native CLI, browser classes and WASM bindings. Native and browser engines use vendored Argon2 C. Local terminal/stdin/page input; optional Rust/Python launcher serves a checked HTML page on loopback without processing wallet secrets. Conditional build/release jobs prepare drafts. Evidence: src/lib.rs:1, build.rs:1, src/bin/mhfe/main.rs:224, src/bin/mhfe/serve.rs:219, packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py:307, .github/workflows/release.yml:100.
assets: Passwords, mnemonic phrases, BIP39 passphrases, entropy, recovered states and wallet keys (src/password.rs:23; src/memory.rs:35).
Browser package and release integrity (web/runtime.js:266; src/bin/mhfe/serve.rs:169; .github/workflows/release.yml:120).
trustBoundaries: Direct CLI: main hardens/isolate before startup and prompts; menu uses isolated command threads, with no separate network namespace (src/bin/mhfe/main.rs:224-246,289; src/bin/mhfe/menu.rs:277,312-333). Existing stdin/stdout/terminal descriptors remain usable; explicitly exported plaintext goes to chosen stdout recipient. Linux seccomp limits sockets/io_uring and Landlock new filesystem mutation; inherited descriptors are not revoked (src/bin/mhfe/protect.rs:268,574,611). Serve requires network/writes and vector generation writes (src/bin/mhfe/main.rs:322).

Rust to native C: checked lengths and layout, bounded allocation callback, synchronous pointer lifetimes and error wipe; library callers do not acquire CLI sandboxing (src/engine/ffi.rs:43-192,365-380; src/lib.rs:32,39; build.rs:9,22). WorkFactor PIM 0..1023/memory 0..21 defaults to 2 GiB reusable area and twelve rounds (src/suite.rs:85,87,120; src/engine/native.rs:63).

Page to workers: page supplies worker source/WASM; checked startup/build identifiers, owned Uint8Array copies transferred, failed transports wipe copies, workers terminated after completion/cancel (web/runtime.js:173,206,266,475,508,665,697). Page/browser retain authority over secrets; workers are responsiveness/lifetime boundaries.

Explicit Rust serve file selects parent/mhfe-fast-mode.sha256, requires plain listed basename matching selected file and digest before reading once into RAM (src/bin/mhfe/serve.rs:120,142,169,219). Menu discovery uses actual executable parent plus checked listed HTML (src/bin/mhfe/serve.rs:107). Python chooses explicit file or script parent/listed HTML, reads checksum beside selected page (packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py:278,320,330,333).

Rust/Python servers bind 127.0.0.1 port 0, permit only GET/HEAD '/', exact single Host 127.0.0.1:<port>, 16 connections/16 KiB heads/10 second request and response deadlines. Browser launch receives public URL only (src/bin/mhfe/serve.rs:41,55,227,275,400; packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py:35,124,192,342).

Browser build assembles dist/runtime WASM/worker/runtime, dist/core engine/client and independent classes then stamps identifier/manifest (scripts/build-wasm.sh:94-112). Docker stages validated repository-local canonical-output[-suffix]/release, verifies SHA256SUMS before replacement (scripts/build-reproducible.sh:4,17,30,40,51). Release job depends on checks/builds, verifies release/* archive checksum coverage, attests and creates --draft --verify-tag with docs/releases/<tag>.md; write/OIDC/attest authority is separate from PR CI ( .github/workflows/release.yml:100-135).
attackerCapabilities: May tamper with container, repair input and public API settings without knowing password or owning trusted deployment files.
Local programs/websites can attempt loopback requests, but only public static page is served (src/bin/mhfe/serve.rs:400).
Embedding page already receives secrets; hostile code with page authority is not independently contained by worker.
Trusted build/maintainer compromise requires additional authority; adjacent checksums/build identifiers cannot authenticate against replacement of both.
securityObjectives: Bound/validate password and work parameters (src/password.rs:23,56; src/suite.rs:120).
Require supported confirmation before rekey sealing (src/rekey.rs:233,260).

Reduce native secret exposure via hardening, wiping, bounded buffers, best-effort locks and accurately reported restrictions (src/bin/mhfe/main.rs:226; src/memory.rs:170; src/bin/mhfe/protect.rs:268).
Restrict loopback serving and reject mixed package/release artifacts (src/bin/mhfe/serve.rs:169,227,400; web/runtime.js:266; .github/workflows/release.yml:120).
assumptions: Generated model from independent architecture review verified against consumers; no user-supplied model.
Experimental construction lacks independent cryptographic review; test results do not establish construction security (SECURITY.md).

Native mlock failure warns and operations continue; Windows/browser have no locking; dependency/compiler/browser-string copies and abrupt termination remain best effort (src/memory.rs:4,170; SECURITY.md).
Linux/platform/kernel restrictions limit new access; inherited descriptors and prior threads remain usable, library hosts own sandboxing.
Same-length and 24-word original recovery lacks built-in authentication; 16-bit source check is weak confirmation and not accepted alone for rekey.
Loopback CSP only frame-ancestors 'none'; stronger script/connect policy is embedding-page responsibility (src/bin/mhfe/serve.rs:55).
No remote service or tenant boundary established; terminal logging, kernel availability and embedding integrity are environmental prerequisites.
Checksums/build identifiers detect consistency only; maintainer OpenPGP signing/publication is separate and not runtime verified.

limitations: Security-focused full-scope audit with incomplete execution; no security certification, complete-source claim or release acceptance.
No independent cryptographic analysis of the experimental construction.
Full-cost Argon2/vector replays, real-browser runtime, Windows/macOS tests, canonical builds, live advisory lookup, external pin authentication and published release verification not executed.

Most production boundaries reviewed; some large wallet helper/test/vector bodies, vendored headers, developer-only tools and historical documentation were not fully audited. Exact remaining scope is retained in coverage.
Native memory locks and isolation are platform/kernel dependent and best effort; inherited descriptors remain usable. Browser strings cannot be reliably erased.
Same-length containers and 24-word originals lack built-in recovery authentication. The 16-bit source check is a filter, not strong wallet identity confirmation.
Original library test log was truncated in tool output; its exact summary is retained as an excerpt. Command start/end UTC timestamps were not independently captured.
Initial wrong-toolchain failure and sandbox socket failures retained separately from corrected checks. Reruns are not added to overlapping totals.
